audit.whatIsWrong: Full-layer chart rows 0-3 read Skill while content win[] and the packet say Viktor.
audit.why: TF has no early kill threat and farms with Wild Cards; Viktor owns levels 1-5, it evens at 6 on Destiny tempo, Viktor takes over at 2+ items.
audit.corrected: Four side-alone edits with rewritten whys (win[] already correct).

audit.why: Spikes right: Viktor's 3-5 dominance, TF's 6 (Destiny 170s CD, Gate 5500 range), skill at first item on conversion, Viktor late.

audit.whatIsWrong: "Death Ray" for Viktor's E across seven content fields; missing interactions: Pick a Card can cancel Viktor's channel-flagged R, and TF's combo opens on the W auto-reset tell.
audit.why: Riot's E text names the Hextech Ray. Kit flags TF W as hardCC + autoReset; Viktor R is interruptible.
audit.corrected: Renamed throughout; channel-vs-gold-card sequencing added to breakdown.cooldowns. 'Gold Card' suspectName is a false positive (real Pick a Card selection).

audit.why: Pick a Card 6s, Destiny 170/140/110s, Viktor W 17s.
dosFull[1].d and dontsFull[2].d were verbatim tradeGood/tradeBad under unrelated titles.
audit.corrected: Rewritten to match their titles with kit numbers.

edits.before: Q-shield trades on his last-hits — the empowered auto walk-away is sneakily one of the better level-1 trades mid.
edits.after: TF has no level-1 kill threat — your autos and range control the lane while he last-hits with Wild Cards.

edits.before: E online: the laser farms AND pokes in one cast. Aim it through minions into his chest on every wave contact.
edits.after: E online: laser farms AND pokes in one cast — he must Wild Cards the wave, so every contact is your free trade.

edits.before: Full kit: W zones his aggression and the E-Q-auto trade pattern is fully armed. Stack your first augment quietly.
edits.after: Full kit and still yours: your E out-ranges his poke and the Q-shield wins every step-up. Stack augments quietly.

edits.before: Lost Chapter timing — laser every wave contact and bank Manaflow. Each augment makes the same spells quietly crueler.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 stay yours: out-poke and out-shove him before Blue Card sustain and level 6 flatten it — bank the CS lead.

edits.before: - Twisted Fate Pick a Card (Gold): matchup-defining — The locked gold card starts every trade and gank — back off the moment it glows yellow. Read it like a second minimap. - Guard your W Gravity Field like a fifth summoner spell. - Ultimate goes to kill windows only.
edits.after: - Pick a Card (W) is a 6s cooldown — the locked gold card starts every trade and gank; back off when it glows yellow, and never channel R into it. - His Destiny is 170s at rank 1: one window of roams, then it is gone. - Your W is 17s — guard it like a fifth summoner.

edits.before: E through the wave into his chest, Q-shield the response, empowered-auto, and walk — a full trade where his answer hit a shield.
edits.after: His stun needs 200 range — Gravity Field on his approach path means the gold card walk-up ends stunned before he swings.

edits.before: Casting E at melee-adjacent range against a loaded engage — Viktor's cast times are an assassin's favorite metronome.
edits.after: Destiny reveals you anywhere and Gate lands in 1.5 seconds — at half HP a jungler plus gold card is lethal; reset first.

edits.before: At 3 your Death Ray out-ranges his poke and your shield wins every step-up trade.
edits.after: At 3 your Hextech Ray out-ranges his poke and your shield wins every step-up trade.

edits.before: You dominate this window: Death Ray out-ranges his Wild Cards (Q) and your Siphon Power shield eats his poke, so every time he steps up to farm you clip him with an E and win the trade. Punish him hard before he stacks Blue Card mana sustain.
edits.after: You dominate this window: Hextech Ray out-ranges his Wild Cards (Q) and your Siphon Power shield eats his poke, so every time he steps up to farm you clip him with an E and win the trade. Punish him hard before he stacks Blue Card mana sustain.

edits.before: You scale far harder into two-plus items; evolved Death Ray plus Chaos Storm out-damage his pick potential, and he becomes a utility Gold-Card bot while you carry teamfights.
edits.after: You scale far harder into two-plus items; evolved Hextech Ray plus Chaos Storm out-damage his pick potential, and he becomes a utility Gold-Card bot while you carry teamfights.

edits.before: You control levels 1-2 outright: Twisted Fate has no early kill pressure and must last-hit with Wild Cards, which lets you free-poke him with autos and set up your Death Ray angle. Keep the wave slightly on your side so he has to walk into your range for caster minions. He is a farm-and-scale pick early, so deny him tempo now while he is weakest.
edits.after: You control levels 1-2 outright: Twisted Fate has no early kill pressure and must last-hit with Wild Cards, which lets you free-poke him with autos and set up your Hextech Ray angle. Keep the wave slightly on your side so he has to walk into your range for caster minions. He is a farm-and-scale pick early, so deny him tempo now while he is weakest.

edits.before: Levels 3-5 are all yours: Death Ray out-ranges Wild Cards, your Siphon Power shield trades up on his poke, and you can shove him in and threaten every step he takes toward the wave. Build a CS and HP lead here because it flattens at 6. Ward the sides so that when Destiny comes online you already know where he wants to go.
edits.after: Levels 3-5 are all yours: Hextech Ray out-ranges Wild Cards, your Siphon Power shield trades up on his poke, and you can shove him in and threaten every step he takes toward the wave. Build a CS and HP lead here because it flattens at 6. Ward the sides so that when Destiny comes online you already know where he wants to go.

edits.before: From level 6 on the matchup becomes about tempo, not the duel — you still beat him head-to-head, but his Destiny plus Gate roams equalize the map, so it comes down to who converts pressure first. Into two-plus items you out-scale him decisively: evolved Death Ray and Chaos Storm out-damage his pick kit, and he fades to a Gold-Card utility role while you take over fights.
edits.after: From level 6 on the matchup becomes about tempo, not the duel — you still beat him head-to-head, but his Destiny plus Gate roams equalize the map, so it comes down to who converts pressure first. Into two-plus items you out-scale him decisively: evolved Hextech Ray and Chaos Storm out-damage his pick kit, and he fades to a Gold-Card utility role while you take over fights.

edits.before: Poke him down with Death Ray every time he walks up for CS
edits.after: Poke him down with Hextech Ray every time he walks up for CS

notes: Chart: win[] matched the packet, so rows 0-3 got side-alone edits with rewritten whys. 'Gold Card' suspectName is a false positive — it is the real Pick a Card gold selection, not a misname. Missing interactions covered: never-channel-R-into-gold-card added to breakdown.cooldowns; the W auto-reset burst tell is already the substance of dosFull[0] ('back off the moment it glows yellow') so no extra edit. dosFull[2].d says 'fifteen-second invitation' for a 6s Pick a Card — overstated, but the field is under-25-char-exempt? It is not; flagged here rather than edited since the invitation framing includes the re-lock and choose time and I could not verify a precise effective number. Death Ray -> Hextech Ray consistent with the ryze/taliyah/talon proposals.
